item.title: What's the latest on Julian Sayin? Here's what Ryan Day said
item.description: Ohio State coach Ryan Day said quarterback Julian Sayin is still expected to miss several weeks after he was injured at Indiana . “They're still going through some of their testing and meetings,” Day said during an appearance on the “Buckeye Roundtable” on 97.1 The Fan on Oct. 19. Day provided no other update on the status of Sayin beyond reiterating the timeline. Sayin left with an injury during the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes’ 19-15 win over the Hoosiers on Oct. 17 and did not return. When Indiana defensive lineman Mario Landino sacked Sayin on a first down just past midfield, he collided into his arm. The hit sidelined Sayin, who went into the locker room at Memorial Stadium and later emerged with his right arm in a sling. Day first mentioned that Sayin would miss several weeks during his postgame news conference, indicating there would be a significant change at quarterback. Sayin has been behind center for the Buckeyes throughout two seasons, making 21 consecutive starts since beating out Lincoln Kienholz in a preseason competition as a redshirt freshman in 2025. Kienholz spent last season as the backup behind Sayin before he transferred to Louisville, leaving Ohio State with less experience on the depth chart. Luke Fahey, a freshman from Southern California who replaced Sayin at Indiana, is in line to start after emerging as the backup over Tavien St. Clair, a former five-star recruit from Bellefontaine. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X. item.title: When Giants’ J.J. McCarthy could start for New York, according to Ian Rapoport
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images When Giants’ J.J. McCarthy could start for New York, according to Ian Rapoport appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the decision for the New York Giants to go with either J.J. McCarthy or Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback, the conversation stems from the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. While McCarthy’s time is seemingly coming for the Giants, this NFL insider discusses when that could be the case. In the loss to New Orleans, Winston threw for 152 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, leading New York to put McCarthy in the game after trading for him from the Minnesota Vikings in late September. Coming into the game in the fourth quarter, he showed flashes, throwing for 243 yards with a touchdown and interception, with Ian Rapoport saying to Jeremy Fowler on the NFL Network that they could wait a week because of the Houston Texans’ defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I would not expect a decision until the New York Giants really have time to kind of let this breathe and really just figure out the various factors at stake, and one of those factors…they face the Houston Texans’ pass rush,” Rapoport said. “They are good. Now, the defense hasn’t been quite as stingy as it has in the past, but Will Anderson playing like one of the top players in the NFL, regardless of position. Danielle Hunter is balling as per usual, and that be the situation you would put J.J. McCarthy out in, and while not knowing how up to speed he is on the protections and essentially keeping him out of harm’s way.” Examining how the Giants might play the QB situation (with @RapSheet ) pic.twitter.com/kyXazISKv8 — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 19, 2026 J.J. McCarthy to see “significant snaps” for the Giants While McCarthy may not be starting for the Giants on Sunday against the Texans, “significant snaps” are coming for the 23-year-old this season. “Here’s what we learned yesterday in the fourth quarter for the New York Giants. J.J. McCarthy’s time is coming. Whether it’s this week, whether it’s after the bye, we don’t know that for sure,” Rapoport said. “J.J. McCarthy is going to play significant snaps for the Giants this season.” At any rate, it remains to be seen who New York head coach John Harbaugh picks to start Sunday against Houston. item.title: Aaron Rodgers' brother shares sweet family moment at Steelers game
item.description: Aaron Rodgers' brother shares sweet family moment at Steelers game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aaron Rodgers' brother, Luke Rodgers, shared a snapshot of a special moment with their family over the weekend. Luke came to support Aaron during the Pittsburgh Steelers matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18. "Last weekend was pretty special," Luke captioned the photos with his brother and children at the game. Aaron commented on the post, " Planes, trains, and renegade! also misspelled cakes." "The best weekend!" Luke's wife, Aimee, commented on the post. "Also, I want to be sure everyone knows, I cut a huge slit down that poncho, so Bella was only covered by my hand and not by any plastic! I feel like I need to be proactive about that." The photos showed the family wrapped in plastic ponchos to combat the rainy and windy weather during the game. Aaron posed with his niece Evie and nephew Jack on the sidelines. Luke and Aimee have three children after recently welcoming their baby girl in August. The post also showed some clips of the children cheering on their uncle in the suite as they rocked their Steelers gear. Luke added some at-home moments as well, celebrating a birthday and Aaron playing with trains with Jack. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Luke Rodgers (@thelukerodgers) The photo follows Aaron's own post with his parents, Luke, and his niece and nephew in July. The Steelers quarterback spoke about what it meant to him to have his family by his side after a years-long estrangement. “I’m happy to be reunited, and that part of my life is a really beautiful addition, and I gotta give my wife a lot of credit for — not that she was pushing me because she never was — but just the way she loves and supports me, having her by my side throughout this process has been really special, and I miss those relationships,” he recalled in conversation with NFL Network’s Kyle Brandt. “It’s been really beautiful to reconnect with them — all of them,” he said. “I got to spend a long weekend recently with my parents … my brother and his sweet wife and their incredible two kids. I got to be an uncle.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aaron Rodgers (@aaronrodgers12) While Luke shared photos of the family, Aaron revealed that he will "never" post them again . “There’s been a narrative out there,” he said, referencing news about the strained relationship with his family per USA Today. “There’s not been a lot of information that’s truthful about it. And I think that the personal life should stay personal and private." “But I feel like it was part of the full-circle to just one time post something, and never again,” he added. “So that that narrative can finally be put to rest.” This is Aaron's last season in the NFL after 22 seasons. The Steelers' next game will be on Sunday, Oct. 25 against the New Orleans Saints. More lifestyle news: Angel Reese

item.title: Yankees could target Brewers All-Star if David Bednar leaves in free agency
item.description: Yankees could target Brewers All-Star if David Bednar leaves in free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees ' bullpen may look totally different in 2027. Six of their relievers will soon become free agents, including closer David Bednar. The Yankees can extend him a qualifying offer, which would bring him back to New York for at least one season if he accepts. Bednar is one of the more consistent closers in baseball, converting 35 of 39 saves this season. It would be a major loss for the Yankees if he decides to sign with another club. Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote that this will be a huge offseason for New York's bullpen roster construction. "With David Bednar and darn near every other reliever of note hitting free agency, the Yankees have quite a bit of work to do on their bullpen. The dream target would be Mason Miller, if the Padres are willing to have that conversation," Miller wrote. He identified Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill as someone the Yankees should target if they fail to re-sign Bednar. "But while trading for Devin Williams didn't pan out how they hoped in 2025, going back to Milwaukee for Trevor Megill could be the move. He was an All-Star last year and probably ought to be a three-time reigning All-Star at this point," Miller added. MORE : White Sox reportedly have 'no urgency' to sign Munetaka Murakami to an extension Megill throws a power fastball and nasty knuckle curve, which helped him punch out 69 batters in 61.2 innings in 2026. He reaches free agency in 2028, and the Brewers have a history of trading their stars one year before they hit the open market. Josh Hader and Devin Williams (both traded) were in identical contract situations as Megill. item.title: Utah AD Mark Harlan on ‘College GameDay,’ late kickoffs and more
item.description: University of Utah Athletics Director Mark Harlan speaks during a town hall at Rice-Eccles Stadium's in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Aug. 16, 2025. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News It’s an exciting week for the University of Utah. The No. 10 Utes, one of just six college football teams that are still undefeated, are gearing up for the biggest game of their season so far — a late-night matchup against No. 14 Houston. Saturday’s Utah-Houston clash is one of the premier games on the Week 8 schedule and is one of just two ranked-vs-ranked games on the slate, No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas being the other. Since “College GameDay” already visited Austin this year and Texas lost last week, it made Salt Lake City a no-brainer choice for the traveling pregame show. The “GameDay” production crew won’t have to travel very far to set up shop. After airing live from BYU ahead of the Cougars’ win over Notre Dame, “GameDay” will make the short drive up I-15 to set up in Salt Lake City for the third time in four years. “GameDay,” which draws millions of viewers each week, will essentially be a three-hour advertisement for the university and the football program. “Anytime we get to show off our campus and our student body and everything’s great about Salt Lake City, University of Utah, I think it’s fantastic for the nation to see,” said Utah coach Morgan Scalley While “GameDay” presents another good opportunity to pitch Utah to the nation, the best pitch for the program won’t come on the pregame show, it’ll come during the game. “I think the biggest recruiting tool you have is winning games,” Scalley said. “That’s the biggest recruiting tool you have. So our players understand that it’s all about game day and what they do on the field and the best thing they can do to maximize the ”College GameDay" experience is to win.” “... Yes, it can be a lot of fun, but ultimately at the end of the day, it’s only fun if you win that game.” Hosting “GameDay” has become old hat for the University of Utah. Saturday will mark the seventh “GameDay” broadcast from Utah’s campus. In 2004, the first time the show originated from Utah, Scalley was a senior safety and ESPN’s pregame show kicked off a day that saw Utah close out an 11-0 regular season with a 52-21 pummeling of BYU. “If you want to know who the first rhino was, it was Steve Fifita. He scored a touchdown in that game as they handed the ball off to him,” Scalley said, referring to the defensive tackle’s punctuating touchdown in that game. Two decades later, Scalley is the head coach of Utah and “GameDay” is coming back yet again. “I really want to thank coach Scalley and this staff and this football team for giving us this incredible opportunity with ESPN ‘GameDay’ coming in,” said Utah athletic director Mark Harlan. “I think it’s remarkable. There’s not a lot of schools out there that have been able to host three of the last four years. There’s some in the Big Ten and SEC would dream of that, but we’ve got it here at Utah.”

The show starts at 7 a.m. MDT and runs until 10 a.m. The final hour features Rece Davis, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban and Kirk Herbstreit, along with a to-be-announced guest, selecting the day’s games. The show is free to attend and there will be free parking available. “GameDay” broadcasting from the state of Utah two weeks in a row speaks volumes to the excellent programs in the Beehive State. “I think what’s going on in the state of Utah in football is remarkable,” Harlan said. “That story I imagine is going to be told pretty profoundly. To have two teams here in the top 10 in this era is just incredible. Listen, we all know, I mean, I’m really close with Kalani (Sitake). He’s awesome. “And what Morgan’s doing, I mean, it’s remarkable. I’m on the CFP (committee), so I’m watching every game, but I certainly have been watching them and watching a lot of other teams. But to see both teams win in this way and be undefeated, it’s remarkable.” As exciting as it is for “GameDay” to be in Salt Lake City, it’ll make for a long day for Utah fans. Kickoff for Saturday is set for 8:15 p.m. MDT on ESPN. Saturday will mark the fourth time this season that Utah has been scheduled for an 8:15 p.m. kickoff. Three of those games have come at home, though the Kansas game scheduled for 8:15 p.m. was moved up to 6 p.m. due to forecasted inclement weather. The Pac-12 built a brand on “after dark” games, but the conference actually had rules about how many late-night games each team could play. item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 05: Manager Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees gestures as he walks out to the mound during the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the American League Division Series at Tropicana Field on October 05, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. According to an MLB writer on Oct. 19, the Yankees might target an American League rival. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) Stephen Parello of FanSided revealed his latest New York trade proposals, naming the Yankees as a potential destination for Carlos Correa of the Houston Astros . In exchange, they would package Ryan McMahon up and ship him out to the Lone Star State. “Swapping Carlos Correa for McMahon helps the Astros, but as a standalone move, most of that help doesn’t come until 2028,” Parello wrote. “The trade that brought Correa back to Houston was facilitated by the Twins paying down approximately $11 million per year of his salary, bringing it down to $20 million per season through his option years, which begin in 2029.” This move would — or should — raise concerns for New York, primarily because of Correa’s injury history. “For the Yankees, Correa is an injury risk, and he’s no longer the 25-to-30-homer bat that he was in his younger days,” Parello further noted. Now in his age-32 season, the veteran infielder is on the tail end of his professional career. During his 2026 campaign, he slashed .279/.369/.418 with a .787 OPS and just three homers through his 32 game appearances. In 2025, he slashed .276/.332/.402 with a .734 OPS through 144 games, split between the Minnesota Twins and the Astros. In July 2025, the Twins traded him to Houston with cash in exchange for minor leaguer Matt Mikulski. item.title: Nick Sirianni on Eagles allowing Jalen Hurts to play, fly home from London with known blood clot: 'We leave that up to the medical experts'
item.description: As details continue to emerge regarding Jalen Hurts' blood clot and the decisions by the Philadelphia Eagles to allow him to play and fly overseas with it, so does scrutiny around those decisions. Head coach Nick Sirianni faced said scrutiny on Monday in the form of a news conference . He was asked repeatedly about how the Eagles went through their decision process in initially managing Hurts' blood clot in his calf. Hurts has since been diagnosed with bilateral pulmonary emboli, which means he has blood clots in both lungs. Sirianni: 'I'm not a medical expert' Each time he was asked about the topic, Sirianni cited "medical experts" on Philadelphia's staff while declining to divulge details about what conversations were had with whom and how the team's decisions regarding Hurts were made. "I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni said Monday when asked if the Eagles should have managed Hurts' condition differently. "I lean on our guys in all those situations. "I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It's not just me that has major care for our players. It's them as well." Sirianni faced this questioning after it was revealed Hurts' diagnosis had worsened since he played and traveled overseas with the blood clot in his calf. Nick Sirianni repeatedly cited Eagles "medical experts" when asked Monday about decisions regarding Jalen Hurts' health. ASSOCIATED PRESS Jalen Hurts' diagnosis worsened after he played in, flew home from London game The Eagles announced Monday morning in a joint statement with Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn that Hurts had been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. They announced that his "prognosis is very good" and that he's expected to "make a full recovery." They did not announce a timeline for his return to football, but Hurts will miss the rest of the season, per multiple reports . News broke later from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, who reported that Hurts had been advised by doctors not to sleep in the 36 hours prior to the game as a medical precaution, and that he acted on that advice. Pelissero's since walked that report back, and, in part due to conflicting reports, it's not clear how much Hurts did or didn't sleep before playing the Jaguars. But one thing is clear. item.title: NBC schedules USC-Ohio State on Halloween for fifth-straight Trojans primetime game
item.description: Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images Traditionally, when you think of NBC and college football, you think of Notre Dame. The USC Trojans are apparently working to change that perception. The Big Ten announced kickoff times and broadcast information for Week 9 games on Monday, with the big Saturday, Oct. 31, showdown between USC and the Ohio State Buckeyes set for 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. This is the first time the two teams will meet as Big Ten members and the first time the Buckeyes will play on NBC this season. The Trojans have been NBC’s primetime team of choice since their Sept. 26 loss to the Oregon Ducks. They followed that with wins over Washington on Oct. 3 and Penn State on Oct. 10. They’ll travel to Wisconsin for their Oct. 24 primetime showdown, ahead of the OSU game. As a reminder, under the arrangement among Big Ten media partners Fox, CBS, and NBC, the networks hold a draft each year with a predetermined number of selections to decide which Big Ten games they’d like to broadcast that season. Fox always gets the top three picks and five of the first 11, while CBS and NBC each get three of the top 11 and switch off at No. 4 each season. Notable Oct. 31 TV selections: Wisconsin-Iowa: Noon FOX ND-Navy: Noon ABC/ESPN ASU-Texas Tech: Noon ABC/ESPN Florida-Georgia: 3:30 ABC Minnesota-Indiana: 3:30 CBS ASU-BYU 3:30 FOX Ohio St-USC: 7:30 NBC Miss St-Texas: 7:30 ABC/ESPN Miami-UNC 7:30 ABC/ESPN — Stewart Mandel (@slmandel) October 19, 2026 As for why NBC is going all-in on USC, there are some obvious reasons. First, as the Big Ten’s primetime game rights holder, NBC is usually limited by which teams it can access. Fox usually gobbles up all the Ohio State (and Indiana now) home games. Since the Buckeyes are on the road here, Fox can’t pull rank and claim this one. Second, under the Big Ten arrangement, no USC home game can kick at noon ET, so Big Noon is out. That tends to make the Trojans more available for the evening than traditional Big Ten programs. Third, Oregon is on the way down, and USC is on the way up. The unranked Ducks have lost two of their last five games and barely held off Nebraska last week. Meanwhile, USC is 6-1 and No. 16 in the nation. NBC could look to undefeated No. 9 UCLA but, all due respect to the Bruins, they don’t command a TV audience like USC, at least not yet. And their upcoming schedule is a bit of a snooze compared to the Trojans. So NBC is smartly riding the USC wave on their will-they-or-won’t-they drive back to the College Football Playoff, as long as it keeps going. If the Trojans come out of this stretch without another blemish, there won’t be much reason to look elsewhere. item.title: Commanders Share Awful Injury Update on RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt
item.description: Washington Commanders rookie running back Jacory-Croskey Merritt has rushed for 671 yards so far this season. Getty The Washington Commanders won’t have one of their most dynamic offensive players for the next month, if not longer. As the Commanders prepare for a Monday Night Football showdown with the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers, they shared some downer injury news about running back and leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt. “Good news: The Commanders have activated CB Trey Amos from IR, as well as LB Jordan Magee and RB Jeremy McNichols,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on Monday. “Bad news: RB Jacory Croskey – Merritt Is headed to IR with a groin injury.” “Washington has placed RB Jacory Croskey – Merritt on IR along with OLB Javontae Jean-Baptiste,” ESPN’s John Keim wrote on X. Croskey-Merritt has rushed for 239 yards and 2 touchdowns through five games, but is averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing tie against the New York Giants in Week 5 — a game in which the Commanders watched the clock run out instead of attempting a 41-yard, game-winning field goal. Croskey-Merritt Led Commanders in Rushing in 2025 Croskey-Merritt, a 2025 7th-round pick, led the Commanders with 805 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns as a rookie after starter Austin Ekeler was injured (torn Achilles tendon) and another key running back, Brian Robinson Jr., was traded before the season. The Commanders initially believed Croskey-Merritt would only miss the 49ers game. “Sources: RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt expected out for Week 6,” Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account on Saturday morning. “Commanders plan to rule Croskey-Merritt out for the 49ers game, per source,” ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler wrote on his official X account on Saturday. Commanders RB Issues Seem Partly Self-Inflicted While the Commanders’ running back injuries are no one’s fault, their lack of depth is certainly the team’s fault. It seems everyone is hurt, and the running back who could have stepped in and made an impact — 2026 draft pick Kaytron Allen — was released by the Commanders on October 8 in a surprise move and immediately claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins . By signing Allen so quickly — and given the short time he was with the Commanders — it’s hard not to see this move as Washington basically giving the Dolphins a free draft pick. “New Dolphins RB Kaytron Allen ran for 4180 yards, on 5.4 per carry, and 39 TDs in 4 years at Penn State,” The Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson wrote on his official X account. “Dolphins continue collecting rookie draft picks cut by other teams. They essentially added a 5th rounder ( Justin Joly ) and 6th rounder (Allen) when other teams quickly moved on.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Commanders Share Awful Injury Update on RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt appeared first on HEAVY .

One was veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who missed last week’s game with a hamstring injury. Commanders Get Major News on Diggs Hours before kickoff, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Diggs, after practicing for several days this week, is trending toward playing against San Francisco. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty The Anaheim Ducks return to the ice on Monday night, looking to rebound as they square off against the New York Rangers. Ville Husso will get the nod to man the Ducks’ net, as reported by Stephen Whyno and Daily Faceoff. Husso has seen action in two games this season, with one start. He’s 1-0-0 and is currently rocking a .935 save percentage and a 1.58 GAA. In his lone start in 2026-27, Husso made 27 saves on 29 shots against the Calgary Flames. Husso, however, will face a greater challenge on Monday. The Flames were struggling to put goals up when he faced them, but the Rangers are a bit of a different story. New York is 11th in goals scored with 28 through 10 games. That said, they are coming off a shutout loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets, and have scored just once in their previous two contests. It was the second time an opponent shut out the Rangers this season, with the first coming in their season opener to the Boston Bruins . New York rebounded following that matchup, defeating the Tampa Bay Lightning 5-1. Offensively, the Ducks will face Dylan Garand, as Daily Faceoff and Vincent Mercogliano have confirmed. Garand has played well filling in for the injured Igor Shesterkin, posting a 3-2-1 record, a .927 save percentage, a 1.81 GAA, and a shutout. He could give the Ducks’ scorers a challenge. Anaheim Ducks Projected Lines And Pairings Against Rangers Daily Faceoff and Zach Cavanagh have Alex Killorn, Leo Carlsson, and Nikita Klepov taking the first line. Carlsson continues to pace the Ducks in scoring with nine points and two goals through seven matchups. Mikael Granlund appears to be returning after missing the previous matchup vs. Boston. Before going down with an injury, Granlund was on a tear , scoring at least one point in his first six matchups. He is slated to man the second line with Frank Vatrano and Beckett Sennecke at the wings. Roger McQueen is slated as the third-line center, with A.J. Greer and Cutter Gauthier taking the wings. Gauthier played the previous game at center in Granlund’s absence, but struggled to win draws . And finally, Tim Washe looks to center Jeff Malott and Judd Caulfield. Washe has been rather productive, with four points and two goals in seven games. As for the defensive pairings, Jackson LaCombe is projected to line up alongside Noah Warren. LaCombe continues to put together a solid campaign early on, with six points and a goal in seven games. Tyson Hinds and Tristan Luneau look like the middle pair, while Pavel Mintyukov and Nick Jensen are the projected third pair. item.description: The Rams have placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he suffered a knee injury in Week 6 Getty The Rams have placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he suffered a knee injury in Week 6 Getty The Los Angeles Rams are officially in panic mode after suffering an ugly 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. With a 2-4 record, the presumed Super Bowl favorite entering the season is trending in the wrong direction, and it’s becoming abundantly clear that changes need to be made. Entering this game, the Rams were rolling with a new kicker, Blake Grupe, after Harrison Mevis was released in the wake of their overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. Grupe didn’t even make it through a quarter of action with L.A. before he was forced out of the game with a knee injury, which prompted L.A. to make a roster move involving him. Rams Place Blake Grupe on Injured Reserve LA Rams Transactions: • Reserve/Injured K Blake Grupe pic.twitter.com/eiyLAZ82GF— Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 19, 2026 Special teams has been a longstanding issue for Los Angeles, and that has stood true to begin the 2026 campaign. Mevis took over as the Rams’ kicker midway through last season, but after hitting just five of his nine field goal attempts through his first five games this season (which included a pair of misses against the Bills), the team opted to move on from him. Mevis’ replacement ended up being Grupe, who had spent the beginning of the season on the New York Jets practice squad. Early on against the Cardinals , Grupe seemed to indicate that he was a significant upgrade over Mevis, as he easily converted a 44-yard field goal on his first kick for his new team. On the ensuing kickoff, though, Grupe badly hurt himself when attempting to tackle Devin Duvernay , and he was quickly ruled out of the game with a knee injury, forcing Los Angeles to get through the rest of the game without a kicker. It looks like the team will have to find a new kicker for the second straight week, as Grupe was placed on injured reserve Monday afternoon. Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
